name: spellkave_bind_actor
label: Bind Actor (verb)
description: #1968 verb-UX round 6: bind an already-placed actor's identity (actor_identities, upsert-by-entity_key) and, optionally, grant it one or more capabilities (actor_capabilities) in a single call — folds the genesis-window self-grant idiom (an identity bind + a `frontier.apply_manifest` grant, the `srd/regdar`/`phandelver/hero` pattern every ad-hoc live-authored actor bundle needs post-core/player-retirement) from 2 spellkave_write_rows calls into 1. `entity_key` must already carry an actor_spatial_locations row (workspace, live, or the active target) — place it first via spellkave_place_actor (mirrors spellkave_define_behavior's own `grant_to` precondition). #1968 workspace idempotency: re-authoring the SAME entity_key's identity bind REPLACES it (never duplicates — the server itself upserts on (actor_id, identity), and every corpus fixture binds one entity_key to exactly one identity); each capabilities[] grant upserts by (actor_entity_key, capability_id, source), mirroring add-capability-grant.

bundle.description: bundle_id stamped on every generated row. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (#1968 smart default).

entity_key.description: entity_key of an already-placed actor (e.g. via spellkave_place_actor) — must already carry an actor_spatial_locations row (workspace, live, or the active target); this call does not place one.

identity.description: actor_identities.identity. Default '$sender' resolves to whoever submits the applying delta. Pass a concrete identity hex string only when binding to a KNOWN, fixed identity instead.

role.description: actor_identities.role. Default 'primary' (the corpus-dominant value; 'dm' is the one observed override). NOT a cosmetic label: r_claim_actor refuses every value but 'primary', so authoring 'dm' deliberately makes the seat un-self-claimable — right for a human DM anchor handed over by the operator, wrong for a programmatic seat that wants the self-claim path. It never affects visibility or write authority, which come from the capability grant alone.

capability_id.description: actor_capabilities.capability_id — must already resolve to an authored capability_definitions row (workspace, live, or the active target); this call does not auto-create it. Privileged frontier.* ids use spellkave_grant_role with an explicit role and extent.

source.description: actor_capabilities.source. Omit for the schema default 'manifest' (mirrors `add-capability-grant`'s own default). This is grant provenance, not authority over a role or extent.

capabilities.description: actor_capabilities grants issued to the SAME entity_key, alongside the identity bind. Default `[]` (identity-only bind — no grant). Ordinary capability rows are supported; frontier.* capability requests are refused with a pointer to spellkave_grant_role.
